page.layout: Running head at top, centred. Below it, one column of text: a continued paragraph, then a decorative border, a heading across two lines, and the main paragraphs with a short closing passage. One marginal note block in the right margin, beside the first paragraph. Left margin fragments are show-through from the neighbouring page and are not transcribed.

l.i: cipium reale per accidens, quod ad principia-
tum refertur ex respectu quodam extrinseco
& accidentario.
Sic collegimus varias sententias de principiis,
quae satisfacere possunt iis, qui contenti sunt
perfunctoria rei alicujus cognitione. Non sane iis, qui
intimam rerum cognitionem venantur. Fateor,
praclara sunt, quae commemoravi ex aliis, mutatis
mutandis, & ordine commodiori adhibito. Sed &
hoc fateor, magnis illis viris non propositum fuisse,
ut omnium disciplinarum principia perstringerent.
Hoc enim si illis cura fuisset, peculiarem de principiis
disciplinarum tractatum scripsissent. Iccirco
ego primus aggrediar, Duce Jehovâ, plenissimum
evulgare hac de re tractatum. Nolo hic attingere
principia physica, nolo metaphysica percensere,
nolo principia complexa tantum commemorare.
Omnium disciplinarum principia paucis tra-
dere volo. Tu, studiose lector, fave
meis conatibus, eisq; bene
precare.

note.i: Judicium authoris de hucusq; tra-ditis sen-tentiis.

page.notes: The decorative border between the continued line and the heading is an ornament, not text. The right-margin note is set in small type across four lines; it is transcribed as one note with its printed hyphens. Left-margin fragments are show-through and were omitted. Doubtful readings: "praclara" and "eisq;" (the abbreviation mark may be a different sign). Spelling kept as printed, including "perfunctoria rei" and "tractatum".
